title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: final settlement amount, rounding and the measure recorded
content:
## Scope

This rule of the Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims product line fixes how the settlement written on an approval is finalised: when the annual aggregate reduces it, where rounding happens, and when the proven loss measure is recorded.

## Rule

1. For a product whose annual aggregate limit is above 0.00, the settlement produced by the liability measure is then reduced to the aggregate still available on the cover: the lower of the two stands. A product whose annual aggregate limit is 0.00 is not reduced.
2. When the aggregate reduced the amount, the approval records the aggregate limit measure.
3. The final amount is rounded to the cent. Apart from the invoice value of the affected packages, the Hague-Visby limit and the declared value share, no intermediate figure is rounded.
4. The approval records the proven loss measure when the amount was not bound by a limit, a share, a cap or the aggregate, including when the invoice value of the affected packages limited the proven loss.

## Input, judgement, output

| Settlement from the measure | Aggregate still available | Product's limit | Amount written | Measure recorded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 18,000.00 | 15,000.00 | above 0.00 | 15,000.00 | Aggregate limit |
| 18,000.00 | 40,000.00 | above 0.00 | 18,000.00 | as fixed before the aggregate |
| 18,000.00 | not measured | 0.00 | 18,000.00 | as fixed before the aggregate |

All figures are hypothetical.

## Hypothetical rounding example

A proven loss of 1,234.56 USD under a hypothetical valuation uplift of 5 percent gives a loss basis of 1,296.288, which is not rounded; less a hypothetical deductible of 300.00 it leaves 996.288, and only this final figure is rounded, to 996.29 USD.

## Points of judgement

**The invoice value of the affected packages cut the claim amount down, and nothing else bound. Which measure is recorded?** The proven loss measure.
